title: Activation Sparring Framework (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of a lightweight cross-team framework for planning and executing staged activations (canaries, micro-A/B, and traffic-slicing) with an emphasis on rehearsal, rapid sparring, and clear stewardship. The word 'sparring' here refers to intentionally pressure-testing rollout plans before real traffic exposure so we reduce surprise failure modes once live.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Small to medium product surface launches (new routing, model variant swaps, response-format changes).
- Situations where latency/cost/quality tradeoffs are material and multiple teams must coordinate (product, infra, SRE, solutions eng, support).
- Not intended for full platform migrations or infra-only hotfixes (those use the infra runbooks).

Key principles:
1) Rehearse early and often: run a low-fidelity sparring session with synthetic traffic and a stakeholder tabletop at least one week before exposure.
2) Minimal blast radius: start with the smallest meaningful cohort; prefer more micro-steps over large leaps.
3) Ownership clarity: one activation steward (single point of accountability), plus defined role backups.
4) Observable contracts: define the top 3 signals and exact thresholds that will trigger auto-rollbacks or manual stop.
5) Fast rollback path: ensure a one-command path exists and has been smoke-tested during sparring.

Glossary (quick):
- Activation steward: owner for the rollout choreography and post-mortem.
- Traffic conductor: person operating the traffic slices and feature flags.
- Sparring: rehearsal and chaos-lite exercise to surface gating and comms issues.
- Safety clamps: pre-configured limits (e.g., % traffic, rate limits) that prevent runaway exposure.

Roles & responsibilities (recommended):
- Activation steward: craft hypothesis, own readiness checklist, coordinate stakeholders, sign-off for each expansion step.
- Signal owners: product/ML engineer(s) who own the quality/accuracy metrics.
- Traffic conductor: on-call infra/ops engineer to execute slice changes and monitor.
- SRE observer: monitors infra signals (latency, error budget, queue depth).
- Comms lead: drafts messaging templates for status updates and incident escalation.

Sparring checklist (pre-launch rehearsal):
- Run synthetic traffic matching 2 profiles: baseline (90th percentile behavior) and adversarial (rare/high-cost prompts).
- Execute the rollback flow (simulate a failure and confirm traffic can be pinned back).
- Validate observability: dashboards, alert thresholds, trace context tags present.
- Time-to-rollback measurement: record how long the team needs to reduce exposure to 0%. Target < 3 minutes for critical regressions.
- Confirm on-call contactability matrix and escalation chain.

Activation lifecycle (recommended cadence):
1) Hypothesis + slice design (Activation steward)
2) Sparring rehearsal (synthetic traffic + tabletop)
3) Pilot: 0.1% - 1% traffic for 1-2 hours with extended observation window
4) Micro-step escalations: incrementally double exposure windows (1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8%) with checks at each step
5) Full exposure or sustained steady-state if targets met
6) Post-launch evaluation and permanent routing decisions

Signals and gating examples (pick top 3):
- Quality: user-facing regression rate (e.g., answer-clarity score, human eval drop) threshold: degrade > 4% relative to baseline -> stop.
- Latency: P95 increased by > 80ms absolute or > 30% relative -> hold.
- Cost/Throughput: token/second cost > budgeted per-request baseline by 25% -> alert and investigate.
- Safety: any high-severity safety signal (see safety checklist) -> immediate rollback.

Quick gating matrix (simplified):
- Green: all signals within soft thresholds -> proceed to next step.
- Amber: one non-critical metric exceeded -> pause, investigate 15-30 min, consider reverting small step.
- Red: critical metric exceeded or safety event -> automatic revert to previous stable route and incident kickoff.

Minimal experiment template (fill for each rollout):
- Hypothesis: (one-sentence)
- Success criteria: (quantitative top-3 metrics)
- Slices: (cohorts and sizes)
- Sparring date: (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Pilot window: (start/end)
- Rollback command: (exact CLI/console action)
- Owner contacts: (steward, traffic conductor, SRE, comms)

Comms snippets (short):
- Pre-pilot: "Starting pilot for <feature> at <time>. Pilot slice: X%. Watch signals: <list>. Activation steward: <name>."
- Stop message: "Pilot paused at <time> due to signal <name>. Reverting to stable route. Investigating. Activation steward: <name>."

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How rigid should automatic rollback thresholds be vs. giving human grace for transient spikes?
- When should we fallback to model variants versus reducing traffic?
- Policy for multi-region rollouts where a regional loss might be acceptable but global impact is not.

Next steps (action items):
- Run first cross-team sparring session for the Search rerank reroute by 2025-02-10 (owners: Maya, Priya).
- Add a standardized rollback CLI command to the ops repo and validate in CI. (owner: Liam)
- Pull together a short playbook for customer-facing comms and an escalation phone tree. (owner: Comms lead)

Notes and provenance:
This is intentionally lightweight and designed to slot into existing runbooks. The term "sparring" was adopted to emphasize rehearsal rather than formal dry-run. Feedback welcome — add inline comments or ping the activation-steward channel.

Appendix: quick failure modes to simulate during sparring:
- Model latency step-function from cold-start KV misses
- Tokenization/regeneration loops increasing cost
- Partial downstream dependency timeouts (embedding store hit-rate drops)
- A/B contamination where user cohorts see inconsistent UX due to cookie/multi-device mismatches

End of draft.
